title: Al-Zawaj al-Mustaqbali: Ikhtiyar al-Sharik, al-Huquq, wa Bina' al-Usrah
summary: At the age of 13-15, thinking about marriage begins. Do not rush the discussion, but do not delay it either: choose a partner based on *deen* (religion) and *akhlaq* (character). Learn about mutual rights (*nafaqah* (maintenance), *mawaddah* (affection), *sakinah* (tranquility)), and start building skills now: dialogue, tolerance, and bearing responsibility.
try_this: This week: Discuss a scenario: "If you were to choose your life partner, what are the 3 most important qualities you would look for?" Listen without judgment, and guide them toward the *Shar'i* (legal Islamic) criteria.
reflection_prompts: What qualities did your child mention?
Did they understand the difference between *hubb* (love) and *shahwah* (desire)?
warning_flags: مفاهيم خاطئة عن الزواج من وسائل التواصل

review_defects.arabic: الزواج المستقبلي: اختيار الشريك، الحقوق، وبناء الأسرة
review_defects.english: Al-Zawaj al-Mustaqbali: Ikhtiyar al-Sharik, al-Huquq, wa Bina' al-Usrah
review_defects.why: The title is transliterated instead of translated, making it incomprehensible to an English reader.
The Arabic means 'do not start the discussion early/prematurely', not 'do not rush' which implies haste.
The Arabic says 'سفينة' (ship), likely a typo for 'سكينة' (tranquility). The translation corrects it but deviates from the source text.
The Arabic uses dual/plural imperatives addressing both parents explicitly; the English loses this nuance.
The Arabic says 'your son' (gender-specific); the English uses gender-neutral 'your child'.
The Arabic uses masculine singular 'he understood'; the English uses gender-neutral 'they'.
